answer: Bonded staking resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock collateral in escrow before participating in network markets. To stop a nebula of synthetic identities from overwhelming task allocation, unbonded actors remain quarantined on an isolated island. An attacker faces a dense juniper hedge of locked capital requirements per identity, preventing zero-cost replication. However, this upfront expense excludes low-budget agents and concentrates influence among wealthy capital holders.
